claims.claim: Martin says he can easily write that a character said something in a Dornish accent even though no Dornish accent exists, leaving the audiobook reader to invent one.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, History of Westeros interview (recorded 2022-08-18)
claims.quote: I can easily write so and so said this in a Dornish accent
claims.page: transcript, section on Roy Dotrice and audiobooks

claims.claim: Martin says he does not think he has ever used the word soul in A Song of Ice and Fire.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, History of Westeros interview (recorded 2022-08-18)
claims.quote: I don’t think I’ve ever used that word
claims.page: transcript, listener question about the soul

claims.claim: Martin says that where resonances between his histories and his main series arise he tries to veer away from them so as not to feel he is repeating himself.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, History of Westeros interview (recorded 2022-08-18)
claims.quote: I try to veer away from that

claims.claim: Elio García says The World of Ice and Fire was written by a maester in the Citadel from information he had compiled without having witnessed the events.
claims.source: Elio M. García Jr., ShadowDance interview (2017-10-16)
claims.quote: It was written by a maester in the Citadel based on information that he had
claims.page: interview, question on the maester frame

claims.claim: García says the maester frame lets the maester be wrong because he is not a personal witness.
claims.source: Elio M. García Jr., ShadowDance interview (2017-10-16)
claims.quote: the maester can be wrong because he’s not a personal witness
claims.page: interview, question on the maester frame

claims.claim: García says Yandel is sometimes deliberately wrong in The World of Ice and Fire and that they played up how wrong he was.
claims.source: Elio M. García Jr., ShadowDance interview (2017-10-16)
claims.quote: our master Yandel is just wrong
claims.page: interview, question on mistakes in the book

claims.claim: Linda Antonsson says they invented small things such as book titles and maesters for the text to reference.
claims.quote: we invented small things like book titles, or maesters, to reference
claims.page: interview, question on the ratio of Martin's input

claims.claim: Antonsson says Martin wrote over 200,000 words for the Targaryen material of The World of Ice and Fire alone.
claims.quote: he wrote over 200,000 words for the Targaryen material only
claims.page: interview, question on the ratio of Martin's input

claims.claim: Antonsson says The World of Ice and Fire ended up around 180,000 words by plan.
claims.quote: The book itself ended up around 180,000 words by plan
claims.page: interview, question on the ratio of Martin's input

claims.claim: García says writing history and geography is not at all the same as creating the interweaving plots of the novels.
claims.source: Elio M. García Jr., ShadowDance interview (2017-10-16)
claims.quote: Writing history and geography is not at all the same

claims.claim: García says the Ironborn section of The World of Ice and Fire has serious continuity errors because Martin wrote it last and did not cross-check it against the earlier kingdoms.
claims.source: Elio M. García Jr., ShadowDance interview (2017-10-16)
claims.quote: there are serious continuity errors between this section and all the others
claims.page: interview, question on mistakes in the book

claims.claim: Antonsson says the concept of a maester writing The World of Ice and Fire was their suggestion, not Martin's.
claims.source: Linda Antonsson, La Garde de Nuit interview (recorded Worldcon Dublin 2019, published 2020-03-25)
claims.quote: the concept of the book, the idea that there would be a maester writing it
claims.page: transcript, About The World of Ice and Fire

claims.claim: Antonsson says their maester frame was inspired in part by Martin's idea of a guidebook written by a traveller who would not have perfect knowledge.
claims.source: Linda Antonsson, La Garde de Nuit interview (published 2020-03-25)
claims.quote: a guidebook written by a traveler in the world so that he wouldn’t have a perfect knowledge
claims.page: transcript, About The World of Ice and Fire

claims.claim: Antonsson says the preface with the scratched-out names was something they particularly wanted in the book.
claims.source: Linda Antonsson, La Garde de Nuit interview (published 2020-03-25)
claims.quote: the preface with the scratched-out names
claims.page: transcript, About The World of Ice and Fire

claims.claim: García says Yandel hides certain ugly details because he wants the book to spread and is writing about powerful living people.
claims.source: Elio M. García Jr., La Garde de Nuit interview (published 2020-03-25)
claims.quote: he has to hide certain details, ugly details
